sessions.situation: I have three group projects, and one of them is only taking by myself. I feel like my ability is so limited, I can not make some contributaions, and my own project is using ai.
evidence_for: I don't know how to do front-end and back-end
I can not write them by myself
I didn't learn how to do them
I just ask ai to realize my idea
evidence_against: I can use ai to realize my thoughts, and turn my idea into reality, that can be a kind of ability.
sessions.balanced_thought: Because I have so much work to do, using ai is acceptable, and I can also learn something in the process.
sessions.summary: Okay, let’s wrap up. It sounds like you were feeling worried (55/100) when facing a lot of projects and feeling unsure about your skills, leading to the thought “I have no ability.” We explored how you *were* able to use AI to bring your ideas to life, which is a valuable skill in itself. It seems recognizing this helped you shift your perspective, and your worry has decreased to 45/100. You identified magnification as a thinking pattern at play. Your balanced thought – “Because I have so much work to do, using ai is acceptable, and I can also learn something in the process” – acknowledges the situation and finds a more helpful way to view your abilities. Good work completing this thought record – it takes effort to step back and reflect like this.

llm_summary: This thought record demonstrates a shift from feeling worried (decreasing from 55 to 45) when overwhelmed with projects, to a more balanced perspective. The initial automatic thought, “I have no ability,” appears linked to focusing on skill gaps and comparing yourself to a standard of completing all work independently. Identifying this as magnification was a key step. Recognizing the value in utilizing AI – not as a sign of inadequacy, but as a tool for realizing ideas – allowed for a reframing of abilities. This suggests that acknowledging resourceful problem-solving, even when it looks different than expected, can be helpful in managing difficult feelings.
llm_action_items: Notice situations where you feel overwhelmed by tasks.
When facing a challenge, list *how* you are already responding.
Practice identifying one positive aspect of your approach, even if it feels imperfect.
